title: Recursive polynomial coefficients for minors after adjoining columns
statement:
Fix integers $p,n,r,d\ge0$ and commuting symbols $X_{ij}$ for $1\le i\le p$, $1\le j\le n+d$. An integer polynomial in these symbols means a finite integer linear combination of monomials. For each pair of increasing index lists $I,J$ of length $q=r+d$ in $[p]=\{1,\ldots,p\}$ and $[n+d]$, and each pair $U,V$ of increasing lists of length $r$ in $[p]$ and $[n]$, define integer polynomials $L_d(I,J;U,V)$ by the following finite recursion, with $p,n,r$ fixed. For $d=0$ set $L_0(I,J;U,V)=1$ if $(I,J)=(U,V)$, and $0$ otherwise. For $d>0$, writing $I=(i_1,\ldots,i_q)$ and $J=(j_1,\ldots,j_q)$, set
$$L_d(I,J;U,V)=\sum_{a=1}^{q}(-1)^{a+q}X_{i_a j_q}L_{d-1}(I\setminus i_a,J\setminus j_q;U,V),$$
where deletion preserves order and polynomials on the right use only the first $n+d-1$ columns. Every remaining column index is at most $n+d-1$; for $q=1$ the remaining list is empty. Let $R$ be any commutative ring and $B$ any $p\times(n+d)$ matrix over $R$ [def-weil-matrix], and let $A$ be its first $n$ columns. Evaluating $X_{ij}$ at $B_{ij}$ gives
$$\det(B_{I,J})=\sum_{\substack{U\subseteq[p],\ V\subseteq[n]\\|U|=|V|=r}}L_d(I,J;U,V)(B)\det(A_{U,V}).$$
Here every submatrix uses increasing order [def-weil-submatrix] and its determinant is [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. The identity holds for every such selection, including $r=0$ and $d=0$; if there are no row or column selections the corresponding assertion is vacuous. The polynomials are the displayed recursive data, not coefficients selected from an existential ideal-membership assertion.

proof.text: Fix $p,n,r$. At each stage $d>0$, put $q=r+d>0$. If $J=(j_1<\cdots<j_q)$ lies in $[n+d]$, then $j_{q-1}<j_q\le n+d$ when $q>1$, so deleting $j_q$ gives a list in $[n+d-1]$; when $q=1$ it gives the empty list. Deleting any row gives a list of length $q-1=r+(d-1)$. Thus every recursive call has the required indices. Starting with $0$ and $1$, finite sums and products by signed symbols remain finite integer linear combinations of monomials. Regarding a polynomial in fewer symbols as the same expression in the larger alphabet makes the recursion well-defined.

proof.text: Prove the displayed determinant identity by induction on $d$, simultaneously for every commutative ring $R$, every $p\times(n+d)$ matrix $B$, and every allowed $I,J$. For $d=0$, $B=A$ and exactly the summand $(U,V)=(I,J)$ has coefficient $1$; all others have coefficient $0$. The sum is therefore $\det(A_{I,J})$. This includes $r=0$, since there is exactly one pair of empty lists and its determinant is $1$.

proof.text:
For $d>0$, assume that induction hypothesis for $d-1$ and let $Q=B_{I,J}$, a $q\times q$ matrix. Apply [lem-trf-minor-laplace-coefficient-formula] with $s=1$ and the position-column set $T=\{q\}$. Its row sets are the singletons $\{a\}$ and its signs are $(-1)^{a+q}$. The $1\times1$ determinant is $B_{i_a j_q}$ by the Leibniz definition. The complementary submatrix is exactly $B_{I\setminus i_a,J\setminus j_q}$, with its inherited order. Consequently
$$\det(B_{I,J})=\sum_{a=1}^q(-1)^{a+q}B_{i_a j_q}\det(B_{I\setminus i_a,J\setminus j_q}).$$

proof.text:
Let $B^-$ be the first $n+d-1$ columns of $B$; its first $n$ columns are still $A$. Step 1 puts every complementary minor in the induction hypothesis for $B^-$. Substitute those identities into step 3 and distribute the finite sums. The coefficient of $\det(A_{U,V})$ becomes
$$\sum_{a=1}^q(-1)^{a+q}B_{i_a j_q}L_{d-1}(I\setminus i_a,J\setminus j_q;U,V)(B^-)=L_d(I,J;U,V)(B).$$
The equality is precisely the defining recursion after substituting entries for symbols: substitution in a finite integer polynomial preserves its sums and products. This proves the induction step. No inverses or nonzero elements were used. If $r=0$, the same argument terminates in the empty determinant $1$; if a size-$q$ row or column selection does not exist, there is no identity to check.

Delivery shape: one commit, only the item and the report, 0 new nodes, statement and stmt_deps unchanged, proof_deps equal to the union of the step uses, and no re-split repair note for this item. Step 1: j_q is the maximum of J, so J minus j_q lies in [n+d-1] with length r+(d-1); the recursion is well defined, including q=1 and the case j_q<=n. Step 2: base case d=0 by the Kronecker delta, with r=0 covered because the cited determinant definition gives det(empty)=1. Step 3: the Laplace node with s=1 and T={q} gives the sign (-1)^{a+q}, the 1x1 determinant is B_{i_a j_q}, and the complement in increasing order is B_{I minus i_a, J minus j_q}; only the node's displayed statement is used. Step 4: the induction hypothesis applies to B^- (its first n columns are A), L_{d-1} uses only columns up to n+d-1 so evaluating at B^- equals evaluating at B, and the sum interchange gives exactly the defining recursion. I checked small cases: the 2x2 case r=d=n=1 gives the usual determinant, r=0,d=1 gives B_ij, cases with r>n or q>p are vacuous, and nothing depends on the characteristic or on zero divisors. Duplicate search with rg -L for cofactor, column expansion and Laplace found no node stating this identity. No cycle: the Laplace node has empty proof_deps. No SGA. Advisory only: Mathlib det_succ_column would also give step 3. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem det_submatrix_eq_sum_columnExtensionMinorCoefficient {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (p n r d : ℕ) (B : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin (n + d)) R) (I : Fin (r + d) → Fin p) (J : Fin (r + d) → Fin (n + d)) (hI : StrictMono I) (hJ : StrictMono J) : (B.submatrix I J).det = ∑ U ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin r → Fin p)).filter StrictMono, ∑ V ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin r → Fin n)).filter StrictMono, MvPolynomial.eval₂ (Int.castRingHom R) (fun ij ↦ B ij.1 ij.2) (columnExtensionMinorCoefficient p n r d I J U V) * ((B.submatrix id (Fin.castAdd d)).submatrix U V).det
lean.note: The two definitions supply the literal recursive polynomial data introduced in this node. A fixed ambient alphabet avoids casts between polynomial rings: each recursive call uses only the symbols in its ordered lists, hence only the first n+d-1 columns at the first reduction on valid selections. StrictMono maps Fin k to Fin m encode increasing index lists; the two finite filtered sums enumerate each increasing pair once.
